summary: Exhaust every race-free way to prevent a quorum-lost Primary self-minting a UUID with stock DRBD; rigorously confirm the bug; draft the LINBIT bug report

final.recommended_path:
Ship the bundled-module ARM-guard patch now AND file upstream. There is NO stock, race-free configuration that prevents the rotation without breaking Bedrock's guest I/O:

- on-no-quorum=io-error is the only stock knob that prevents the rotation race-free FOR THE QUORUM-PARTITION SCENARIO (it forces susp_quorum=false at drbd_state.c:2473-2474, so there is no quorum freeze->thaw edge to arm the susp_uuid latch at 2476-2480). But it is disqualified on cost: the same cached_err_io (set at drbd_state.c:896-899 for ONQ_IO_ERROR && !have_quorum) errors EVERY guest bio, read and write, with BLK_STS_IOERR at drbd_req.c:2766 on any quorum loss. Guest filesystems remount read-only / VMs crash on every transient minority partition. Unacceptable for a VM-hosting appliance.
- IMPORTANT correction to earlier framing: io-error does NOT structurally kill the 4466 latch in general. The latch keys on resource_is_suspended() (drbd_state.c:245-254), which also has susp_user / susp_nod / susp_fen contributors that are independent of on-no-quorum mode. io-error only closes the specific quorum-driven freeze->thaw edge. So it is race-free for THIS scenario, but it is not a clean structural disarm of the rotation machinery, and (per the Bedrock caveat) it would require BOTH on-no-quorum=io-error AND on-no-data-accessible=io-error to avoid a stray susp_nod re-arm.
- Every other knob (quorum, quorum-minimum-redundancy, fencing/resource-and-stonith, after-sb-*, on-susp-primary-outdated=force-secondary, all module params, sysfs/debugfs) was exhausted and does NOT disarm the rotation at all: none is consulted at the ARM (drbd_state.c:3096-3099) or at the leaking EXECUTE edges (drbd_state.c:4466-4471 and 4295-4305). DRBD also has no autonomous self-outdate under a hard partition (all four __outdate_myself sites are 2PC/receive-handler gated; force-secondary only fires on reconnect in receive_state()/connect_work() -- a timing race the daemon loses).

Therefore the kernel fix is the only race-free option that keeps guest I/O working. Plan:
(1) Apply the +1-condition PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM guard at drbd_state.c:3097-3099 to the drbd9x source bundled in the Bedrock ISO; build the patched module; re-run the 4-node reproducer (isolate Primary from 2 of 4 so it keeps >=1 peer; confirm NO "new current UUID" dmesg line during the partition; heal; confirm NO full resync). The patch applies cleanly and is well-formed C but has NOT been compiled or runtime-tested -- that gate must pass before ship.
(2) File upstream via the drbd-user mailing list (README.md:45-46 explicitly disclaims GitHub issues/PRs and routes to lists.linbit.com). Send the prose report to drbd-user; follow with a checkpatch-clean [PATCH] (Signed-off-by, kernel style -- the repo enforces checkpatch.pl via .gitlab-ci.yml and git hooks) to drbd-dev, CC drbd-user. Optionally mirror to github.com/LINBIT/drbd/issues for a searchable number to reference from ISO patch notes, but the mailing list is the authoritative channel.
(3) Keep on-no-quorum=suspend-io (do NOT switch to io-error). Do NOT pursue the rejected workarounds: after-sb discard-zero-changes is unsafe once a real dirty bit exists, and drbdadm outdate loses the synchronous in-lock race (it is a userspace round-trip; the guard runs inside the state_rwlock critical section that detects the partition, before __NEW_CUR_UUID is ever set -- exactly why the in-kernel guard wins).

Once a fixed upstream release ships, drop the local patch.

@@ finish_state_change() -- create_new_uuid arming for a lost peer

-				    drbd_data_accessible(device, NEW))

Context (DRBD 9.3.2, HEAD a46cbd9):
- Fix site is the ARM in finish_state_change() at drbd/drbd_state.c:3097-3099 (the lost_contact_to_peer_data branch). Net +2 lines (or +1 folded).
- PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM is set EARLIER in the SAME finish_state_change() pass at drbd/drbd_state.c:2885-2886 (`if (role[NEW] == R_PRIMARY && !have_quorum[NEW]) set_bit(PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM, &device->flags);`) and cleared on quorum return -- so the flag is in scope and authoritative at the arm site. (Note: the susp_uuid EXECUTE edge at drbd_state.c:4466-4471 lives in w_after_state_change(), which runs ASYNC on the drbd_worker thread, NOT in finish_state_change(); that is precisely why guarding the ARM in finish_state_change -- before __NEW_CUR_UUID is ever set at 3134-3136 -- is the correct single choke point rather than chasing the async execute edges.)
- Use PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM (not have_quorum[NEW]) to mirror the existing guarded sibling at drbd/drbd_receiver.c:9884-9888 and to cover both on-no-quorum modes, since the flag is set independent of mode at 2885-2886.

Why the ARM, not the EXECUTE:
- Guarding the ARM stops __NEW_CUR_UUID from being set at 3134-3136, so nothing downstream (the susp_uuid edge at 4466-4471, the peer-D_FAILED edge at 4295-4305, the MAKE_NEW_CUR_UUID worker, the write route) ever sees the bit.

Preserves all legitimate bumps (verified by inspection of the source):
(a) keep-quorum-lose-a-secondary: have_quorum[NEW] is still true at 2885, PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM never set, guard passes -> bump proceeds.
(b) Secondary->Primary promotion: armed at the separate 3131-3132 statement, untouched.
(c) write route: already guarded at drbd_sender.c:3443 (`if (device->have_quorum[NOW] && drbd_data_accessible(device, NOW))`).
The legacy proto<110 sub-branch at 3101-3104 is intentionally left unguarded (no pre-9.0 peers in a quorum cluster; moot).

final.bug_report_markdown:
## drbd-user post (prose report)

**To:** drbd-user@lists.linbit.com  (subscribe: https://lists.linbit.com/listinfo/drbd-user)
**CC (when the patch is attached):** drbd-dev@lists.linbit.com
**Subject:** [DRBD 9.x] Quorum-lost frozen diskful Primary mints a new current-UUID -> false split-brain / full resync on heal (asymmetry vs. the already-guarded write & disconnect routes)

---

### Environment / version (PLACEHOLDERS -- capture on a sim, see commands below)

- DRBD module version: `<drbdadm --version>`  (expected DRBDADM_VERSION ~9.x; bundled source is 9.3.2, git HEAD a46cbd9)
- DRBD kernel module: `<modinfo drbd | egrep 'version|srcversion'>`
- Kernel / distro: `<uname -r>` / `<cat /etc/os-release | head -2>`
- Userspace (drbд-utils): `<drbdadm --version | grep DRBDADM_VERSION>`
- Resource config (relevant options): `quorum all; on-no-quorum suspend-io;` auto-promote no; (fencing/after-sb/on-susp-primary-outdated at defaults). Full: `<drbdadm dump <res>>`

### Summary

On a diskful **Primary** that loses quorum but **keeps at least one peer** (e.g. a 2-of-4 minority that still has a surviving 2PC partner), DRBD generates a **new current UUID** while I/O is frozen and **zero** user writes have been admitted. The rotation is logged as `new current UUID: <hex> weak: <mask>`. Because the UUID diverged with no data change, when the partition heals the peers see mismatched current-UUIDs and trigger a **full resync** (and, depending on topology, a transient false split-brain). Data is not lost, but the spurious resync is operationally expensive and the UUID divergence is cosmetic-but-real.

This is an **asymmetry bug**: DRBD already guards the two sibling routes into `drbd_uuid_new_current()` against exactly this case, but the **state-change (finish_state_change) arming route** reaches the UUID rotation without the equivalent quorum guard.

### Reproducer (minimal, 4-node)

Config: `quorum all`, `on-no-quorum suspend-io` (the default), auto-promote off.

1. 4 nodes connected, one **Primary** (P), three Secondaries, all `UpToDate`.
2. Network-isolate P from **exactly two** of the three peers (P retains 1 peer -> P is in a 2-node minority that still has a 2PC partner). Use iptables/link-down on P's links to those two peers.
3. Observe on P: `drbdadm status <res>` shows `suspended:quorum`; **no** user writes complete (frozen). Despite this, `dmesg`/kernel log on P shows:
   `block drbd<minor>: new current UUID: <HEX> weak: <MASK>`
4. Heal the partition.
5. Observe a **full resync** between P and the peers that were isolated, even though P admitted zero writes during the partition.

**A/B control (the diagnostic asymmetry):**
- **A (this bug):** isolate from SOME peers while keeping >=1 -> UUID rotates (surviving 2PC partner drives the state-change route).
- **B (already correct):** isolate the Primary from **ALL** peers at once -> **no** rotation (no surviving 2PC partner; the disconnect/write routes are quorum-guarded). The fact that B is clean and A is not is the fingerprint of the missing guard on the state-change route.

### Expected vs. actual

- **Expected:** a quorum-lost frozen Primary that admits **no** writes must **not** mint a new current UUID; on heal it should reconnect without a full resync (same intent as the guarded write/disconnect routes and the in-code comment cited below).
- **Actual:** kernel logs `new current UUID: <hex> weak: <mask>` during the freeze; heal triggers a full resync.

### Root cause (source-cited, DRBD 9.3.2 / HEAD a46cbd9)

The new-current-UUID rotation is a two-stage machine: **ARM** a per-device flag, then **EXECUTE** the rotation later. There are three ways the flag gets to a write of the UUID; **two are quorum-guarded, the third (state-change) is not.**

**ARM (unguarded for quorum) -- `drbd/drbd_state.c:3096-3099`, inside `finish_state_change()`:**
```c
if (lost_contact_to_peer_data(peer_disk_state)) {
    if (role[NEW] == R_PRIMARY && !test_bit(UNREGISTERED, &device->flags) &&
        drbd_data_accessible(device, NEW))
        create_new_uuid = true;
```
`drbd_data_accessible(device, NEW)` short-circuits to `true` on a local `D_UP_TO_DATE` disk (`drbd/drbd_state.c:6384-6385`) -- which a frozen quorum-lost Primary still is -- so a quorum-lost Primary satisfies this branch. **`have_quorum` / `PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM` is not consulted here.** The flag is then set at `drbd/drbd_state.c:3134-3136`:
```c
/* Only a single new current uuid when susp_uuid becomes true */
if (create_new_uuid && !susp_uuid[OLD])
    set_bit(__NEW_CUR_UUID, &device->flags);
```

**EXECUTE (unguarded) -- `drbd/drbd_state.c:4466-4471`, inside `w_after_state_change()` (async, drbd_worker thread):**
```c
if (!susp_uuid[OLD] && susp_uuid[NEW] &&
    test_and_clear_bit(NEW_CUR_UUID, &device->flags))
    new_current_uuid = true;

if (new_current_uuid)
    drbd_uuid_new_current(device, false);
```
(A second leaking execute edge exists at `drbd/drbd_state.c:4295-4305` on a peer `D_UP_TO_DATE -> D_FAILED` transition.) Three lines above, at `drbd/drbd_state.c:4463`, the code reads `have_quorum[OLD] && !have_quorum[NEW]` to fire the `quorum-lost` helper -- so the quorum state is demonstrably available on this path -- yet the UUID rotation itself is not gated on it.

**The asymmetry -- the two sibling routes ARE guarded:**

- **Write route -- `drbd/drbd_sender.c:3443-3444`** (`drbd_check_peers_new_current_uuid()`):
  ```c
  if (device->have_quorum[NOW] && drbd_data_accessible(device, NOW))
      drbd_uuid_new_current(device, false);
  ```
- **Disconnect route -- `drbd/drbd_receiver.c:9884-9888`**, with an explicit multi-line comment (the lead instruction reads verbatim `therefore do not create the new UUID immediately!`):
  ```c
  /* ... But when we lost quorum we are going to finish those
     requests with error, therefore do not create the new UUID
     immediately! ... */
  if (!list_empty(&resource->transfer_log) &&
      drbd_data_accessible(device, NOW) &&
      !test_bit(PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM, &device->flags) &&
      test_and_clear_bit(NEW_CUR_UUID, &device->flags))
          drbd_check_peers_new_current_uuid(device);
  ```

The guard variable used by the disconnect route, `PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM`, is set **earlier in the same `finish_state_change()` pass** at `drbd/drbd_state.c:2885-2886`:
```c
if (role[NEW] == R_PRIMARY && !have_quorum[NEW])
    set_bit(PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM, &device->flags);
```
So at the ARM site (3097-3099) the flag is already in scope and authoritative. This is an **incomplete guard / oversight**, not a missing capability: the state-change route simply lacks the `!PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM` check that its two siblings already carry.

### Precedent (same harm class)

The 9.3.2 ChangeLog (`ChangeLog`, "All fixes from 9.2.18") lists verbatim:
> Fix when a diskless primary creates a new current UUID, fixing possible silent data divergence later

That fix is a cluster of 4 commits inside the **diskless** else-if arm of `drbd_uuid_new_current()` (`drbd/drbd_main.c:5278-5302`); it fixed a *missing* bump and added **no** quorum guard. The frozen Primary here is `D_UP_TO_DATE` and takes the **diskful** arm (`drbd/drbd_main.c:5275`), which that fix never touched. So this is **not** "the diskless variant of the same rotation" -- I cite 9.2.18 only as evidence that **LINBIT already treats an uncontrolled new-current-UUID bump as a correctness / silent-data-divergence bug**. The load-bearing argument is the two guarded siblings vs. the unguarded state-change route above.

### Impact

- Spurious **full resync** on every heal of a minority-but-not-fully-isolated quorum-lost Primary -- expensive on large devices, and exactly the partition pattern a VM-hosting HA appliance hits on transient network blips.
- UUID divergence with **zero** admitted writes -> a false data-divergence signal (false split-brain risk under some topologies).
- Data is **not** lost (writes were frozen), but the operational cost and the cosmetic UUID divergence are real.

### Suggested fix (1-condition, at the ARM)

Guard the ARM in `finish_state_change()` so the flag is never set for a quorum-lost Primary -- this is the single choke point upstream of all execute edges, and `PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM` is already set in the same pass (2885-2886):

```diff
--- a/drbd/drbd_state.c
+++ b/drbd/drbd_state.c
 			if (lost_contact_to_peer_data(peer_disk_state)) {
 				if (role[NEW] == R_PRIMARY && !test_bit(UNREGISTERED, &device->flags) &&
-				    drbd_data_accessible(device, NEW))
+				    drbd_data_accessible(device, NEW) &&
+				    !test_bit(PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM, &device->flags))
 					create_new_uuid = true;
```

This mirrors the existing `drbd_receiver.c:9886` idiom, covers both `on-no-quorum` modes, and preserves every legitimate bump: keep-quorum-lose-a-secondary (PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM never set), Secondary->Primary promotion (armed separately at `drbd_state.c:3131-3132`, untouched), and the write route (already guarded). It must **not** be applied to an EXECUTE edge, because `drbd_state.c:4466-4471` is a shared funnel that also carries the legitimate promotion bump, and `drbd_state.c:3804-3807` is the legitimate fencing/`all_peer_disks_outdated` resume path.

When sending the patch to drbd-dev, it will be a checkpatch-clean `[PATCH]` with `Signed-off-by` (the repo enforces checkpatch.pl via `.gitlab-ci.yml` and the `misc/pre-commit` hook).

---

So under the canonical quorum-loss scenario the flag arms but the UUID write is blocked. NOTE the function drbd_uuid_new_current() itself (drbd_main.c:5273-5304) has NO quorum check -- the gate lives only in its callers. Two direct callers in drbd_state.c bypass the sender gate: 3804-3807 (after-fencing, all_peer_disks_outdated -> fence handler succeeded, an alternative safety mechanism to quorum) and 4466-4471 (when susp_uuid newly set). This IS inside finish_state_change (defined drbd_state.c:2817 "static void finish_state_change(...)", body 2817-3343; next fn abw_start_sync at 3345). In finish_state_change, have_quorum is the local "bool *have_quorum = device->have_quorum;" (line 2837), and the set_bit target is device->flags (PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM is a device flag enum, drbd_int.h:596).
- drbd_state.c:4463 DOES read have_quorum: "if (role[NEW] == R_PRIMARY && have_quorum[OLD] && !have_quorum[NEW])" -> drbd_maybe_khelper(device, NULL, "quorum-lost").
- At the actual fix site (susp_uuid false->true edge, drbd_state.c:4466-4471, plus 4295-4305) BOTH guards are genuinely in scope: have_quorum (local) and device (for test_bit(PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM, &device->flags)). The enclosing for(n_device...) loop spans 3958-4475, and both the have_quorum decl (3963) and device decl (3960) live inside it, so the fix the doc proposes is implementable. PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM persists because it was set on device->flags (the live device object), not a snapshot.

WHY IT IS REFUTED (the false part):
- Line 4463 is NOT in finish_state_change. It is in a DIFFERENT function, w_after_state_change, defined at drbd_state.c:3940 ("static int w_after_state_change(struct drbd_work *w, int unused)"). finish_state_change ends at line 3343, ~600 lines before 4463.
- These two functions are not "the same pass": finish_state_change runs synchronously (___end_state_change calls it at drbd_state.c:832), whereas w_after_state_change is QUEUED to the worker and runs asynchronously on the drbd_worker thread — queue_after_state_change_work() sets "work->w.cb = w_after_state_change;" then "drbd_queue_work(&resource->work, &work->w);" (drbd_state.c:796-798). So 2885-2886 and 4463 execute in separate function invocations on a different thread, not "earlier in the same finish_state_change pass."
- The two have_quorum variables even have DIFFERENT sources: finish_state_change uses "device->have_quorum" (drbd_state.c:2837); w_after_state_change uses "device_state_change->have_quorum" (drbd_state.c:3963, the captured state-change snapshot). They are distinct locals in distinct scopes.
- This exact error is already flagged in the claim's own parent material: lesson_drbd_uuid_rotation_quorum.md line 16 ("the bump runs async on the drbd_worker thread, not synchronously in finish_state_change") and docs/drbd-uuid-quorum-foundations.md lines 72-73 ("It runs in w_after_state_change, asynchronously on the drbd_worker thread"). The verified claim text contradicts that correction by placing the 4463 read "in the same finish_state_change pass."

Net: the in-scope conclusion holds, but the claim is refuted as written because line 4463 (and the 4466 fix site) live in w_after_state_change, not finish_state_change, and run async on the worker thread — there is no shared "finish_state_change pass" linking 2885-2886 to 4463.

verdicts.claim: io-error suppression is structural not timing: susp_quorum only set under ONQ_SUSPEND_IO (drbd_state.c:2473-2474); resource_is_suspended (245-254) excludes cached_err_io; susp_uuid[NEW]=true set in EXACTLY ONE place (drbd_state.c:2480) on the suspended->unsuspended edge. Therefore io-error => latch never arms => EXECUTE at 4466 never fires.
verdicts.evidence:
Verified against LINBIT/drbd 9.3.2 HEAD a46cbd9 in /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd. The three structural sub-facts are all TEXTUALLY CONFIRMED, but the blanket conclusion ("io-error => latch never arms") OVERGENERALIZES and is REFUTED.

SUB-FACTS (all CONFIRMED):
1. susp_quorum gated on ONQ_SUSPEND_IO -- drbd_state.c:2473-2474: "resource->susp_quorum[NEW] = resource->res_opts.on_no_quorum == ONQ_SUSPEND_IO ? !resource_has_quorum : false;". Under on-no-quorum io-error this is forced false. CONFIRMED.
2. resource_is_suspended excludes cached_err_io -- drbd_state.c:245-254: "bool rv = resource->susp_user[which] || resource->susp_nod[which] || resource->susp_quorum[which] || resource->susp_uuid[which]; if (rv) return rv; return is_suspended_fen(resource, which);". No cached_err_io term. CONFIRMED.
3. susp_uuid[NEW]=true in exactly one place -- grep of all "susp_uuid[NEW] =" assignments yields only: :580 (copy from NOW), :2480 (=true), :4526 (=false). The only true-assignment is :2480, inside the edge guard at :2476-2477 "if (!resource->susp_uuid[OLD] && resource_is_suspended(resource, OLD) && !resource_is_suspended(resource, NEW))" with ":2479 if (test_bit(NEW_CUR_UUID...))". CONFIRMED.

WHY THE CONCLUSION IS REFUTED: The latch at :2476 keys on resource_is_suspended(), which has FOUR contributors besides susp_quorum -- susp_user, susp_nod, susp_fen, susp_uuid (:247-253). Each is independent of the on-no-quorum mode:
- susp_nod: set true at :2470-2471 gated ONLY on "on_no_data == OND_SUSPEND_IO" (orthogonal to on_no_quorum).
- susp_user: set via __change_io_susp_user (:5737), driven by drbdadm suspend-io/resume-io and handshake merge (drbd_receiver.c:6785) -- no quorum-mode dependency.
- susp_fen: set via __change_io_susp_fencing (:5758) / :2200, driven by fencing policy -- no quorum-mode dependency.
Separately, the NEW_CUR_UUID flag the latch consumes is armed at :3134-3136 "if (create_new_uuid && !susp_uuid[OLD]) set_bit(__NEW_CUR_UUID...)" (promoted to NEW_CUR_UUID at :906-908), where create_new_uuid is set ENTIRELY by disk-state/role/peer-disk transitions (:3096-3132, e.g. lost_contact_to_peer_data + R_PRIMARY + drbd_data_accessible at :3096-3099; S->P at :3131) with NO on-no-quorum dependency.

Consequence: under on-no-quorum io-error, a resource can still go suspended->unsuspended via susp_user/susp_nod/susp_fen while NEW_CUR_UUID is set, satisfying :2476-2477, setting susp_uuid[NEW]=true at :2480, so the EXECUTE at drbd_state.c:4466-4471 ("if (!susp_uuid[OLD] && susp_uuid[NEW] && test_and_clear_bit(NEW_CUR_UUID...)) ... drbd_uuid_new_current(device, false)") DOES fire. The 4466 latch is therefore NOT structurally dead in io-error mode.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE (the defensible narrower claim): io-error closes ONLY the quorum-loss freeze->thaw edge -- the exact edge captured in docs/drbd-uuid-quorum-foundations.md section 3 ("susp-io( no -> quorum )" then thaw). That edge depends on susp_quorum, which :2474 forces false under io-error; with no quorum freeze there is no quorum-driven suspend/unsuspend transition, and the write path returns -EIO instead (drbd_req.c:670 "if (device->cached_err_io) { ok = 0; ...}", :700 "m->error = ok && quorum ? 0 : (error ?: -EIO)", :2766 cached_err_io -> BLK_STS_IOERR). So for the specific quorum-partition scenario the claim's intuition holds, but the suppression is NOT structurally total -- it is specific to the quorum edge, not to "the latch" in general.

Manpage (drbd.conf-9.0, manpages.debian.org): on-no-quorum values are suspend-io | io-error, default freeze (suspend-io); on-no-data-accessible values io-error | suspend-io. These are independent options, confirming susp_nod can be active while on-no-quorum=io-error.

NOTE: the foundations doc itself (Bedrock/docs/drbd-uuid-quorum-foundations.md section 5b/6) still lists the :4466/:4295 leak as TODO and proposes guarding on PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM / have_quorum[NOW] -- a guard that, unlike the io-error config, would block ALL arming edges. That corroborates that io-error is not treated as a complete structural fix even in the project's own analysis.

verdicts.claim: io-error cost VERIFIED: drbd_req.c:2766 `if (device->cached_err_io || bio_bad(...)) { bio->bi_status = BLK_STS_IOERR; bio_endio(bio); return; }` errors ALL guest bios (read+write) on quorum loss; cached_err_io set at drbd_state.c:896-898 for ONQ_IO_ERROR && !have_quorum.
verdicts.evidence:
Both source trees (/tmp/drbdsrc/drbd and /home/tommy/projects/drbdsrc_clone/drbd) are DRBD 9.3.2 at HEAD a46cbd9, identical. Every line cited in the claim is verbatim-correct.

1) ERROR PATH (read+write) — /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_req.c:2766-2770:
  `if (device->cached_err_io || bio_bad(device, bio)) {`
  `    bio->bi_status = BLK_STS_IOERR;`
  `    bio_endio(bio);`
  `    return;`
  `}`
This is inside drbd_submit_bio() (starts line 2748), which is THE block-device entry point: drbd_main.c:182 registers `.submit_bio = drbd_submit_bio`. So every guest bio enters here. The cached_err_io check at 2766 fires BEFORE any read/write branching — the only direction-specific code after it is the size-zero-read workaround at 2778 (`bio_op(bio) == REQ_OP_READ && bi_size == 0`), which comes later and does not exempt normal reads. The READ short-circuit at 2662-2663 inside drbd_reject_write_early (called at 2756) only skips the *not-Primary WRITE rejection* for reads; it returns false and falls through to the cached_err_io check. Hence cached_err_io errors BOTH reads and writes. The struct field comment confirms intent — drbd_int.h:1641: `bool cached_err_io; /* complete all IOs with error */`. The completion path also enforces it: drbd_req.c:670 `if (device->cached_err_io) { ok = 0; req->local_rq_state &= ~RQ_POSTPONED; }` — i.e. when cached_err_io is set, requests are NOT pushed to the retry queue, they hard-fail.

2) SET CONDITION — /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_state.c:896-899 (exact):
  `device->cached_err_io =`
  `    (o->on_no_quorum == ONQ_IO_ERROR && !device->have_quorum[NOW]) ||`
  `    (o->on_no_data == OND_IO_ERROR && !drbd_data_accessible(device, NOW)) ||`
  `    resource->fail_io[NEW];`
The first disjunct is exactly the claim: ONQ_IO_ERROR && !have_quorum. (The claim quoted lines 896-898; the full statement spans 896-899, the trailing fail_io clause being an additional OR-term the claim omits but does not misstate.)

3) ENUM — drbd-headers/linux/drbd.h:73-76: `enum drbd_on_no_quorum { ONQ_IO_ERROR = OND_IO_ERROR, ONQ_SUSPEND_IO = OND_SUSPEND_IO };`. on_no_quorum is the parsed `on-no-quorum` resource option (drbd_genl.h:150, drbd_req.c:697, drbd_main.c:3712).

ADVERSARIAL CHECK — the one caveat (claim is still CONFIRMED because it explicitly gates on ONQ_IO_ERROR): this error-IO behavior is NOT the default. drbd_limits.h:320-321: `/* By default freeze IO, if set error all IOs as quick as possible */` and `#define DRBD_ON_NO_QUORUM_DEF ONQ_SUSPEND_IO`. The Debian drbd.conf-9.0 manpage agrees: "By default DRBD freezes IO on a device, that lost quorum. By setting the on-no-quorum to io-error it completes all IO operations with an error if quorum is lost." So on quorum loss the io-error completion only happens when on-no-quorum=io-error is explicitly configured; the stock default (suspend-io) freezes/suspends IO instead. The claim's phrase "on quorum loss" is therefore conditional on that config — which the claim itself encodes via the ONQ_IO_ERROR precondition, so it is not a contradiction. Could not refute any factual element: the file:line citations, the BLK_STS_IOERR behavior, the read+write coverage, and the set condition all match the source exactly.

verdicts.claim: No autonomous self-outdate under hard partition: all __outdate_myself sites are 2PC/receive-handler gated, and on-susp-primary-outdated=force-secondary only fires in receive_state() at reconnect — a timing race the daemon loses, same class as the rejected drbdadm-outdate workaround.

Verified against DRBD 9.3.2 HEAD a46cbd9 (both /tmp/drbdsrc and /home/tommy/projects/drbdsrc_clone are byte-identical for drbd_state.c and drbd_receiver.c).

THERE ARE EXACTLY 4 __outdate_myself CALL SITES (drbd_state.h:155 decl; def at drbd_state.c:5786). All four are gated; none fires autonomously under a hard partition:

SITE 1 — drbd_state.c:5854, in do_twopc_after_lost_peer(): "if (phase == PH_COMMIT && (reply->primary_nodes & ~directly_reachable && !pri_incapable))". This is the ONLY site reachable from a purely local trigger (drbd_empty_twopc_work_fn -> twopc_after_lost_peer -> change_cluster_wide_state, scheduled by drbd_schedule_empty_twopc at drbd_state.c:2562 when a peer is lost). It is NOT autonomous-safe by "2PC requires a peer to agree" but by a stronger fact: under a hard partition reply->primary_nodes is ZERO, so the guard is false. Proof chain in change_cluster_wide_state (drbd_state.c:5073): line 5146 "*reply = (struct twopc_reply) { 0 };" and line 5192 "resource->twopc.state_change.primary_nodes = 0;" zero it; reply->primary_nodes is populated ONLY inside "if (have_peers)" (lines 5263/5315). have_peers is set at line 5230 "have_peers = rv == SS_CW_SUCCESS;" from __cluster_wide_request (drbd_state.c:4648), which starts "rv = SS_SUCCESS" (4653) and only upgrades to SS_CW_SUCCESS (4682) inside the per-connection loop AFTER a successful send to a reachable peer; with no reachable peer the loop body is skipped/continues (4665-4668) so rv stays SS_SUCCESS. Thus have_peers==false -> the wait/decision block is skipped -> primary_nodes stays 0 -> at line 5853 "reply->primary_nodes & ~directly_reachable" == 0 -> __outdate_myself NOT called (the else branch at 5855-5863 may even re-promote D_CONSISTENT to D_UP_TO_DATE). PH_COMMIT itself DOES run at line 5369 ("if (rv >= SS_SUCCESS) change(context, PH_COMMIT)") even with no peers, but it is inert because primary_nodes==0.

SITE 2 — drbd_state.c:6084, in do_change_cstate(): "if (phase == PH_COMMIT) { ... if (reply->primary_nodes & ~directly_reachable) __outdate_myself(resource); }". Same driver (change_cluster_wide_state), same primary_nodes==0-under-partition argument; inert without a peer reply.

SITE 3 — drbd_receiver.c:6961, in change_connection_state(): "if (reply && !abort) { ... if (reply->primary_nodes & ~directly_reachable) __outdate_myself(resource); }". Reached ONLY from process_twopc (drbd_receiver.c:7898), which runs ONLY from receive_twopc (the packet handler), registered for P_TWOPC_COMMIT/P_TWOPC_PREPARE in the handler table (drbd_receiver.c:9506-9513). reply->primary_nodes is taken from the incoming packet (drbd_receiver.c:7875 "reply->primary_nodes = state_change->primary_nodes;"). Requires an inbound peer packet -> cannot fire under hard partition.

SITE 4 — drbd_receiver.c:7237, in far_away_change(): "if (state_change->primary_nodes & ~directly_reachable && !(request->flags & TWOPC_PRI_INCAPABLE)) __outdate_myself(resource);". Also reached only from process_twopc (drbd_receiver.c:7901) via receive_twopc. Receive-handler gated; cannot fire under hard partition.

QUORUM-LOSS DOES NOT OUTDATE: On quorum loss the sanitize path sets suspend-I/O, not D_OUTDATED: drbd_state.c:2473 "resource->susp_quorum[NEW] = resource->res_opts.on_no_quorum == ONQ_SUSPEND_IO ? !resource_has_quorum : false;" and the quorum-lost khelper at drbd_state.c:4464; the disk stays D_UP_TO_DATE (frozen). No autonomous D_OUTDATED transition exists on quorum loss. (The only direct change_disk_state(...,D_OUTDATED) is the admin path drbd_nl.c:6212 — the "rejected drbdadm-outdate workaround.")

FORCE-SECONDARY CLAUSE — CONFIRMED, with one refinement to "only in receive_state()": there are THREE force-secondary paths, all reconnect/handshake-gated, none autonomous:
 (a) maybe_force_secondary() at drbd_receiver.c:8341, directly inside receive_state() (the P_STATE handler, registered drbd_receiver.c:9495).
 (b) maybe_force_secondary() at drbd_receiver.c:8116, inside diskless_with_peers_different_current_uuids(), called from receive_state() at drbd_receiver.c:8387.
 (c) A SEPARATE path the claim omits: apply_local_state_change() at drbd_receiver.c:861-867 ("force secondary!", role[NEW]=R_SECONDARY), called from connect_work() at drbd_receiver.c:927/931 with force_demote computed at 913-914 ("resource->role[NOW]==R_PRIMARY && on_susp_primary_outdated==SPO_FORCE_SECONDARY"). connect_work is the reconnection-handshake worker (it calls change_cstate_tag(...,C_CONNECTED,...) and only demotes on SS_HANDSHAKE_RETRY/DISCONNECT/incompat_states). So this too fires only once the peer is reachable again — same reconnect-timing class, not autonomous. The claim's conclusion (force-secondary only on reconnect) is correct; it just under-counts the sites (3, not 1).
maybe_force_secondary itself (drbd_receiver.c:8089-8103) is guarded by "resource->cached_susp && on_susp_primary_outdated == SPO_FORCE_SECONDARY".

DEFAULT/DOCS: drbd-headers/linux/drbd_limits.h:323 "#define DRBD_ON_SUSP_PRI_OUTD_DEF SPO_DISCONNECT" (default is disconnect, NOT force-secondary). enum at drbd-headers/linux/drbd.h:78-80 (SPO_DISCONNECT, SPO_FORCE_SECONDARY). The drbd.conf-9.0 manpage corroborates the reconnect timing verbatim: on-suspended-primary-outdated "is relevant when on-no-quorum is set to suspend-io ... a primary node loses quorum (freezing I/O), then RECONNECTS to another quorate partition that has promoted a different primary with newer data. force-secondary: The node demotes to secondary immediately and fails all pending and new I/O" (default: disconnect; available 9.1.7+). This is exactly the "timing race the daemon loses": the kernel demotes only after the peer comes back, by which point the operator/daemon fencing window has elapsed.

NET: Every __outdate_myself is either receive-handler gated (sites 3,4) or, on the locally-driven 2PC path (sites 1,2), rendered inert by primary_nodes==0 whenever no peer reply is collected — so there is no autonomous self-outdate under a hard partition. force-secondary fires only on peer reconnect. Both halves of the claim hold (minor correction: 3 force-secondary sites, not 1; the gating principle for site 1 is "no peer reply -> primary_nodes==0", which is stronger than but consistent with the claim's "2PC-gated" framing).
